assets.title: Different questions for different requests
assets.content:
Subject: Different questions for different requests
Preview text: Build one intake form that adapts by request type, then test a route into your workflow.

Make one intake form adapt to each request

Hi there,

If your team is rebuilding customer intake, start with one real request flow. Choose the request types, then decide which questions the person actioning each one needs answered.

Tally is an online form builder with conditional logic. You can configure one form to adapt its questions to the request type and the requester’s previous inputs.

That means billing, onboarding and technical requests can follow different paths inside the same form, with the question set designed by your team.

When a suitable destination is available in Zapier’s catalogue, Tally’s published Zapier integration can pass submissions into that downstream app.

Build the first flow and see whether the branching fits your intake process. Tally offers unlimited forms and submissions for free within its fair usage guidelines.

Create a free form → https://tally.so/create

- Tally

asset_metadata.single_idea: Tally lets a CS or Ops team build one intake form that asks different questions for different request types, with a documented Zapier route for sending submissions into downstream tools when a suitable connection exists.

selected_brief.selection_reason: Conditional logic directly addresses the documented intake-design problem: different request types need different information. It gives this reader a concrete operational reason to try Tally, while Zapier provides a documented route into an existing workflow.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team is rebuilding intake, it can use one form to present request-type-specific questions instead of giving every requester the same field set, then use a suitable Zapier connection to pass submissions downstream.
value_case.mechanism: The team configures conditional logic so the form adapts to the requester's inputs. Tally's Zapier integration can connect submissions to apps in Zapier's published catalogue.
decision_conditions: Unlimited forms and submissions are free only within Tally's fair usage guidelines.
The downstream benefit depends on the required destination being available through the documented Zapier catalogue.
The evidence does not establish the depth of any individual connector or field-level mapping into a particular ticketing system.

claim_conditions: Frame the intake situation conditionally rather than asserting that this recipient currently uses a universal form.
Treat the exact question set as a design choice for the team, not an automatic Tally outcome.
Qualify the free offer with Tally's fair usage guidelines.
Build the intake form in the Tally editor (block-based, typing "/" to insert fields), optionally generating or editing it in plain language with Tally AI (E7)
Configure conditional logic so the form branches by request type and collects the fields the actioning team needs (E8)
Connect the form to the downstream destination through the published Zapier integration, or via Tally's API where a team prefers programmatic handling (E9, E10)
Stay within the documented fair usage guidelines to keep unlimited forms and submissions free (E3, E13)

Routing is documented through Zapier's 2,000+ app catalogue and an API; the depth or nativeness of any one destination connector, and field-level mapping into a specific ticketing system, is not established by the selected evidence.

Problem P2 is an inferred audience hypothesis: A single universal intake form fails to collect the specific information that the person actioning a request needs, forcing teams toward request-type-specific forms. Use it only conditionally (if this is relevant to the reader), not as a known current pain, behavior or outcome of the recipient. Product fit does not establish current demand or a demonstrated customer outcome.
Historical sources (2022-12-20); present applicability is not corroborated.
Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

Conditional branching is documented as a mechanism; whether it produces the exact field set each actioning owner wants is a design question, and the source is a single 2022-12-20 discussion whose present applicability is uncorroborated.

Conditional logic can require the same information from an internal submitter as from a customer, but the selected evidence proves no reduction in time-to-resolution or in staff-submitted tickets, and this single undated source describes another vendor's form.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Tally offers an online form builder that would let my team create one free intake form whose questions branch by request type and inputs, then potentially send submissions to a downstream app through Zapier.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly places me on a Customer Success/Ops team revamping intake forms, and the email conditionally says, "If your team is rebuilding customer intake," so the core situation fits without inventing a current tool or failure. The need for request-specific questions is a plausible researched problem, but whether our present forms lose information, use one universal flow, or need Zapier is unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: my Customer Success/Ops team is revamping intake forms at a fast-growing SaaS company.
Email-only: we want billing, onboarding, and technical requests handled within one form.
Email-only: we have or can choose a suitable downstream application in Zapier's catalogue.
Unknown, not asserted as fact: our current intake process asks the wrong questions or causes resolution delays.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Improving intake is relevant now because the profile explicitly says my team is revamping its forms. Collecting request-specific information could prevent handoffs and follow-up, but the profile does not establish that incomplete submissions are currently delaying us or that these three request types are our priority.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I can see the proposed test, but I cannot judge how much setup and maintenance the branching requires or what the resulting experience looks like. The qualified Zapier sentence also leaves me unsure whether submissions can reach the workflow we actually use.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had shown one concrete example of a request-type branch and stated how long that small test typically takes to build.
fixes: Rewrite "Choose the request types, then decide which questions the person actioning each one needs answered" as a concrete miniature example, such as selecting "technical issue" and revealing fields for environment, error message, and screenshots.

Rewrite "When a suitable destination is available in Zapier’s catalogue, Tally’s published Zapier integration can pass submissions into that downstream app" to name a few supported destination examples and clearly say that I should verify whether our own workflow app is supported.
Rewrite "Build the first flow and see whether the branching fits your intake process" to specify the size and expected effort of the suggested first test, without making an unsupported guarantee.

brief.interpretation: Treat this as a one-email acquisition campaign for a new buyer in the selected Customer Success / Ops segment. Because no individual company has been qualified, address teams conditionally when they are rebuilding customer intake rather than assuming the recipient already has the documented problem or a particular software stack.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Customer Success / Ops teams revamping intake forms at fast-growing SaaS companies.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): Customer Success and Operations teams at a fast-growing automation company used a structured form to handle customer support queries and onboarding, as part of an end-to-end process built after the company set its sights on larger enterprise customers.
brief.reader_segment: Customer Success / Ops teams revamping intake forms at fast-growing SaaS companies
brief.promise: Tally can give a CS or Ops team one structured intake form that changes its questions by request type and can pass submissions into downstream tools through Zapier when a suitable connection exists.
brief.orientation: Tally is a no-code form builder a Customer Success or Ops person can use to build a structured customer request/feedback form and pass submissions into the tools their team already works in.
brief.arc: In one email, move from the familiar limitation of universal intake to Tally's concrete conditional-logic mechanism, show the documented downstream route, answer the fit concern honestly, and invite the reader to build one free form.
brief.sequence_rationale: A solution-aware buyer does not need a lesson on why forms exist. The email should lead with the most relevant documented operation: changing the questions according to request type. Zapier then makes the proposition useful within an existing process, while the free offer lowers the cost of testing it. The email must not imply that Tally has already reduced resolution time or staff-submitted tickets, because those outcomes are not established. One applicable objection is addressed: submissions can connect through Zapier's catalogue, but the exact destination connector and field-level mapping still need checking. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign is the unreadable source in a readable form or verification of its missing details.

emails.selection_reason: Conditional logic directly addresses the documented intake-design problem: different request types need different information. It gives this reader a concrete operational reason to try Tally, while Zapier provides a documented route into an existing workflow.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team is rebuilding intake, it can use one form to present request-type-specific questions instead of giving every requester the same field set, then use a suitable Zapier connection to pass submissions downstream.
value_case.mechanism: The team configures conditional logic so the form adapts to the requester's inputs. Tally's Zapier integration can connect submissions to apps in Zapier's published catalogue.
decision_conditions: Unlimited forms and submissions are free only within Tally's fair usage guidelines.
The downstream benefit depends on the required destination being available through the documented Zapier catalogue.
The evidence does not establish the depth of any individual connector or field-level mapping into a particular ticketing system.
